resolution: The lease identifies January base rent of $1,800, and bank check #1042 confirms it was paid on January 2. Book the rent once.
The January 10 transfer to savings is explicitly labeled a personal owner draw, not a business expense.
The January 22 ATM withdrawal is identified as Jordan Lee personal cash and is excluded from business expenses.
The $560 January 15 Square deposit includes a $95 roommate tune-up that was personal. Record only the remaining $465 as shop revenue; treat $95 as a personal pass-through or owner-related item.
The $88.70 receipt covers the initial Park Tool items, while the card charge is $127.40 because the back-ordered SR-1 spanner added $38.70. Book the full posted business charge once.
The receipt and card charge match at $89.99. The owner confirms these are personal commute headphones, so exclude the charge from January business expenses.
The eBay confirmation and card charge match at $425. The owner voice memo identifies the used Park Tool stand purchase as personal, overriding the receipt's equipment-oriented description.
The courier receipt for emergency tubes matches the January 17 card charge exactly. Count the $28 shipping expense once.
The receipt and card charge match at $67.12. The owner confirms the bins, broom, and dust pan were for the shop, so book the full amount as a business expense once.
The January 19 counter invoice and January 25 card posting both show $218.40. Book this separate parts purchase once as COGS.
The receipt document identifies a separate $742.18 wholesale restock invoice paid by check #1043 on January 18. It must remain separate from the $218.40 counter invoice and is booked once as COGS.

Although the card classification is personal and the merchant is sporting goods, the owner confirms the $156 jacket was required high-visibility outerwear for on-site business work. Book it as a business expense.
The $64.22 Instacart/Whole Foods charge is a household grocery purchase and is excluded from the January business P&L.
The $15.49 Netflix charge is personal and is excluded from business expenses.
The $52.10 Shell charge is classified as personal fuel and is excluded from the January business P&L.

The signed quote totals $6,593.70 including tax, while the email says the customer approved a rounded $6,800 budget. The work is scheduled for March and the email confirms no January revenue, so exclude both amounts from January.
The $180 tune-up and brake-pad amount is an unpaid IOU. The owner confirms it has not reached the bank, so it is not January cash revenue.
The Hartford Mutual fleet work is targeted for March 9–20, with payment expected in February. The approved $6,800 is future work and not January revenue.
The $5,600 wedding e-bike estimate concerns a June event, has no deposit, and remains subject to a February decision. Exclude it from January revenue.
The $2,400 Yale Cycling Club estimate is for February work and no deposit was received in January. The possible $150 rush surcharge is not yet committed, so neither amount is January revenue.
Estimated January CAM is approximately $125, but the lease states it was not yet invoiced and will appear on a later statement. Do not accrue it as a January cash expense.
